forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Cheltenham council to fall £563,000 short of minimum reserves by March
news_drafts.lead: Cheltenham's general reserves are forecast to fall to £937,000 by 31 March 2027, leaving the council £563,000 below the level its Section 151 Officer, the chief finance officer, assesses as prudent. An £838,000 forecast overspend is the cause. At the same time, the council's capital programme — money spent on long-lived assets such as buildings — is being cut by 13.5%, from £42.96m to £37.1m. The National Cyber Innovation Centre at Golden Valley, budgeted at £32.85m, is unaffected and now represents 89 per cent of the entire capital spending plan. Separately, the Housing Revenue Account, which manages council housing and is funded by rents, is forecast to overspend by £650,000, driven by £465,000 in lost rental income from vacant properties and £201,000 in additional borrowing costs from higher interest rates.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Housing Revenue Account Capital Forecast, 31 August 2026
findings.headline: Energy Efficiency programme delivering on schedule with full budget spend forecast
findings.detail: The Energy Efficiency & Sustainability Measures scheme for 2030 climate targets is budgeted and forecast at £4.645m (100% delivery). This includes loft insulation, cavity wall insulation, external wall insulation, and heat pump installation.
findings.matters: Demonstrates that at least one major programme is on track to deliver. Shows progress on climate commitments and planned maintenance despite wider programme delivery issues.
findings.quote: Energy Efficiency & Other Sustainability Measures Improving the energy efficiency of the existing housing stock to meet the targets for 2030 - measures include the installation of top up loft insulation, cavity wall insulation, external wall insulation, and new heating systems such as ground source and air source heat pumps 4,645,000       4,645,000

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Housing Revenue Account Capital Forecast, 31 August 2026
findings.headline: Lifts and Warden Call systems showing significant cost overruns
findings.detail: Two schemes show substantial cost increases: Lifts replacement (budgeted £300k, forecast £545.8k, overspend £245.8k or 82%) and Warden Call Upgrade (budgeted £20k, forecast £145.8k, overspend £125.8k or 628%). The Warden Call overrun is particularly acute, suggesting major scope change or cost inflation.
findings.matters: Cost pressures on these programmes indicate inflation, scope change, or unforeseen complexities affecting budget control. The Warden Call overrun (629% of budget) is material relative to the scheme's scale.
findings.quote: Lifts Replacement of passenger lifts and installation of new chair lifts as required 300,000       545,800

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Housing Revenue Account Capital Forecast, 31 August 2026
findings.headline: Kitchen improvements programme forecast to deliver only 41% of £5m budget
findings.detail: The Kitchen Improvements scheme for internal refurbishment is budgeted at £5m but forecast to spend only £2.067m (58% underspend). This is the largest single scheme in the existing property improvements programme and represents substantial underperformance.
findings.matters: Significant underperformance on a flagship programme suggests contractor capacity, supply chain, or programme delivery management issues affecting the council's planned maintenance regime for existing stock.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Housing Revenue Account Capital Forecast, 31 August 2026
findings.headline: Monkscroft School 70-home development only 48% forecast to be delivered
findings.detail: The Monkscroft School land-led scheme for 70 low carbon homes on council land is budgeted at £8.58m but forecast at only £4.15m (52% underspend). This major capital scheme represents one of the council's key housing developments and the shortfall indicates significant delay.
findings.matters: Delay in major housing development affects supply targets and demonstrates delivery capability concerns for a material scheme. The 52% underspend halfway through the year suggests the scheme may not meet its planned timescale.
findings.quote: Monkscroft School Land led scheme for 70 low carbon homes on Council land 8,580,000       4,150,000

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Housing Revenue Account Capital Forecast, 31 August 2026
findings.headline: £9.085m in acquisition schemes (S106 and Market Purchase) forecast to deliver zero spend
findings.detail: Two major acquisition schemes are both forecast at zero expenditure: S106 Purchases (£4.085m for developer-led acquisitions) and Market Purchase (£5m for local market acquisitions). These represent a complete stalling of acquisition activity despite being budgeted at mid-year.
findings.matters: Acquisition schemes are central to the council's housing strategy. Zero delivery represents a significant setback to planned housing supply and signals delays in scheme execution or approvals.
findings.quote: Market Purchase Acquisition of individual properties from the local market to support the wider strategies within the HRA business plan 5,000,000       -
